instruction: Visit https://www.linux.org/ and create a document called "linux_guide.docx" on the desktop. Copy some content about Linux and format at least one section title using a heading style.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires visiting a website, creating a docx document, and applying heading style to at least one section. Evaluator checks if the document contains at least 1 paragraph with a heading style.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator verifies all 4 instruction requirements
Requirement 1 (Visit linux.org in Chrome): Checked via Chrome history getter looking for 'linux.org' URLs in SQLite history database
Requirement 2 (Create linux_guide.docx on desktop): Verified via getter attempting to read file from /home/user/Desktop/linux_guide.docx (returns None if missing)
Requirement 3 (Copy content about Linux): Verified via content_char_count check requiring min 50 characters of non-heading text
Requirement 4 (Format section with heading): Verified via heading_count check requiring min 1 heading-styled paragraph
Heading detection logic is correct: Uses python-docx to check paragraph.style.name for 'Heading' or 'Title' prefix
Content counting logic is semantically correct: Excludes heading paragraphs from content count to ensure actual body text exists
Chrome history logic is robust: Handles multiple OS platforms (Linux/Darwin/Windows), queries SQLite database with LIKE '%linux.org%', gracefully handles errors without failing entire evaluation
Postconfig is appropriate: Activates LibreOffice window and saves document (Ctrl+S) to ensure file is written to disk before verification
Expected values are semantically correct: requires_headings=true, min_headings=1, min_content_chars=50, chrome_history_url='https://www.linux.org/'
